regs_in_letter: FD&C Act misbranding (false or misleading); no CFR section cited in letter text

cases.claim: “…and while I still have CIDP, I have a chance to live vividly.” | “Vyvgart Hytrulo has been proven to significantly reduce the risk of symptoms getting worse.” | “I’m hitting fairways with the fellas. I’m hitting the road with my number one. That’s how we live vividly with Vyvgart Hytrulo”
cases.context: Patients with cane/leg braces shown golfing and driving; trial enrolled INCAT >=2 patients needing walking support; endpoint was time to clinical deterioration.
cases.rationale: Implies all patients can engage in such activities with little functional restriction; not demonstrated.
cases.check: Do depicted activities imply a level of functional recovery beyond what the trial endpoint and enrolled population support?

cases.cat: Misleading presentation of study data (hazard ratio as risk reduction)
cases.claim: SUPER: “For patients identified as responders entering the main part of the study, the risk of arm and leg symptoms getting worse was 61% lower for patients taking VYVGART Hytrulo, compared to patients taking placebo (VYVGART Hytrulo=111 patients; placebo=110 patients).”
cases.context: HR 0.394 for time to first aINCAT increase; absolute risk difference -25.7%.
cases.rationale: Converts a hazard ratio into a '% lower risk' claim, misrepresenting the actual risk reduction.
cases.check: Rule: flag '% lower risk' claims; verify the number is not (1 - hazard ratio) presented as absolute/relative risk reduction.

cases.claim: “And I can treat my CIDP with a once weekly injection in about 30 seconds” with on-screen text “VYVGART Hytrulo (efgartigimod alfa and hyaluronidase-qvfc) a once-weekly self-injection that takes about 30 seconds”
cases.context: Shown while golfing; IFU requires 30 minutes at room temperature, supplies, sharps disposal.
cases.check: Does an administration-time claim omit preparation steps required by the IFU?

cases.claim: Major statement does not communicate allergic reaction emergency symptoms and infusion/injection-related reaction symptoms from the Patient Information.
cases.check: Rule: each W&P in the PPI must appear in the TV major statement.

cases.claim: Multiple scene changes (putting on a golf course, car at crosswalk, woman driving, men walking on golf course, food trucks) and on-screen text (license plate “NMBR 1”) during the major statement.
cases.check: Are there scene changes or extraneous on-screen text during the major statement?
